title: Mass Casualty Triage (START)
summary: For trained responders with more casualties than rescuers: sort everyone quickly into priority groups using walking, breathing, circulation and responsiveness.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} and declare a major incident early
when: Give a METHANE report (see Radio & Comms) and ask for resources

steps.title: Scene safety and report
steps.text: Make the scene safe and send an early report: location, type of incident, hazards, access, number of casualties.

steps.title: Walking wounded → GREEN (minor)
steps.text: Call out: "If you can walk, go to [point]." Those who walk away are GREEN – reassess them later.

steps.title: Breathing?
steps.text: For each remaining casualty: not breathing → open the airway. Still not breathing → BLACK (expectant). Starts breathing → RED (immediate).
steps.caution: Spend under a minute per casualty. Only stop to open the airway or control major bleeding.

steps.title: Breathing rate
steps.text: More than 30 breaths per minute → RED.

steps.title: Circulation
steps.text: No radial pulse, or capillary refill longer than 2 seconds → RED. Control major bleeding now.

steps.title: Mental status
steps.text: Cannot follow simple commands → RED. Otherwise → YELLOW (delayed).

steps.title: Tag, record and re-triage
steps.text: Mark each casualty, keep a count of each colour, and re-triage regularly – casualties change.

doNot: Do not stop to treat one casualty beyond airway and major bleeding during triage
Do not forget to re-triage GREEN and YELLOW casualties
Do not use START unless you have been trained in it – follow your organisation's triage system

sources.body: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
sources.title: CHEMM – START Adult Triage Algorithm

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
